notes.claim: In a fraction the top number (numerator) counts the parts you have and the bottom number (denominator) says how many equal parts the whole is divided into.
A fraction is a number with its own place on the number line, and the whole it is a fraction of can be a shape, a length, a number or a set of objects.
Fractions that look different can name the same number: they sit at the same point on the number line, and multiplying top and bottom by the same number does not change the value.
Comparing fractions is only valid when both fractions refer to the same whole.

sources.title: Breaking down fractions - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The numerator is the number above the line in a fraction and shows how many parts we have out of the whole.

sources.title: Breaking down fractions - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The denominator below the line shows how many equal parts there are in total and so what to divide the whole into.

sources.title: What are fractions? - KS1 Maths resources for Year 2 - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The whole can be a shape, a length, a number or a set of objects.

sources.title: Number & Operations—Fractions | Common Core State Standards Initiative
sources.quote: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

sources.title: Number & Operations—Fractions | Common Core State Standards Initiative
sources.quote: Recognize that the resulting interval has size a / b and that its endpoint locates the number a / b on the number line.

sources.title: Number & Operations—Fractions | Common Core State Standards Initiative
sources.quote: Recognize that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole.

sources.title: An Introduction to Irrational Numbers | NRICH
sources.quote: They occupy the same point on the number line. In a sense, a rational number (the actual ratio) consists of a whole family of equivalent fractions.

sources.title: Fraction
sources.quote: the denominator indicates how many of those parts make up a unit or a whole.

sources.title: Equivalent fractions (video) | Khan Academy
sources.quote: If I multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number, then I'm not changing what that fraction represents.

sources.title: Visualizing equivalent fractions review (article) | Khan Academy
sources.quote: Numbers are equivalent when they are located at the same point on the number line.
